articles.title: Deezer says AI song uploads have nearly overtaken human music
articles.summary: Deezer says it receives almost 75,000 AI-generated song submissions to its music streaming platform each day, which accounts for about 44 percent of all daily uploads.
articles.body: Deezer says it receives nearly 75,000 AI-generated song submissions to its music streaming platform each day, accounting for about 44 percent of all daily uploads, as reported earlier by TechCrunch. Despite the increase in “fraudulent” uploads, Deezer says the consumption of AI songs makes up around 1 to 3 percent of total streams, as the platform continues to remove AI-generated music from its recommendation algorithm. Deezer positions the tool as setting an “industry standard,” adding that the platform is currently the “only” music streaming service tagging AI-generated tracks. The service also demonetizes AI-generated songs and has stopped storing high-resolution versions of them. “AI-generated music is now far from a marginal phenomenon and as daily deliveries keep increasing, we hope the whole music ecosystem will join us in taking action to help safeguard artist’s rights and promote transparency for fans,” Deezer CEO Alexis Lanternier writes in the blog post. As AI-powered song-making tools like Suno and Udio become more popular, music streaming services are dealing with the flood of AI tracks in different ways. While Spotify announced new policies to clamp down on AI-generated music, Apple Music is asking artists and record labels to label songs made with AI. Bandcamp has banned AI music altogether, while Qobuz has started automatically detecting and labeling AI music as well. Since launching its tool in January 2025, Deezer says the number of AI-generated tracks uploaded daily has jumped from 10,000 to 75,000. Deezer has also started allowing other companies to license its AI song-detecting tool. As noted by Deezer, the tool can identify songs made using Udio and Suno, “with the possibility to add detection capabilities for practically any other similar tool as long as there’s access to relevant data examples.” The company is also working on a way for its music detection tool to identify songs without requiring a dataset to train on.

articles.title: MT recebe Semana Nacional de Ciência e Tecnologia com oficinas de IA | G1
articles.standfirst: Programação gratuita inclui atividades sobre inteligência artificial, robótica, sustentabilidade e participação das mulheres na ciência.
articles.summary: Programação gratuita inclui atividades sobre inteligência artificial, robótica, sustentabilidade e participação das mulheres na ciência.
articles.body:
Mato Grosso recebe, entre os dias 21 e 23 de outubro, a 23ª edição da Semana Nacional de Ciência e Tecnologia (SNCT). — Foto: Secom-MT

Mato Grosso recebe, entre os dias 21 e 23 de outubro, a 23ª edição da Semana Nacional de Ciência e Tecnologia (SNCT), com palestras, oficinas e atividades gratuitas sobre inteligência artificial, robótica, sustentabilidade e inovação. O evento será realizado no Centro de Eventos do Pantanal, em Cuiabá , e é aberto a estudantes, professores, pesquisadores e demais interessados. As inscrições podem ser feitas pela página oficial do evento .

A programação inclui debates sobre o uso da tecnologia na saúde, a participação das mulheres na ciência, a preparação dos jovens para o mercado de trabalho e a educação climática. Os interessados podem fazer a inscrição para palestras específicas no site.

Promovido pela Secretaria de Estado de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (Seciteci-MT), o evento também reúne a 18ª Mostra Estadual de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (MECTI) , o 2º Festival Estadual High Tech – Tecnologia, Indústria e Cultura Digital e o 1º Hack Festival Estadual .

A abertura oficial será na quarta-feira (21), às 9h. No primeiro dia, as atividades incluem palestras sobre mercado de trabalho, participação de meninas na tecnologia e proteção de invenções.

Na quinta-feira (22), a programação terá palestras sobre a presença feminina nas áreas científicas e tecnológicas, além de oficinas práticas de inteligência artificial, robótica e sustentabilidade.

Já na sexta-feira (23), os participantes poderão acompanhar atividades sobre agricultura, mudanças climáticas, pesquisa científica e uso de dados na saúde. O evento também terá a premiação dos projetos apresentados na 18ª Mostra Estadual de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação, às 15h.

articles.title: Australian MP Brad Battin shares selfie with Mamitha Baiju as she joins Malayali community for Onam; calls ‘BKU’ actress a ‘down-to-earth superstar’
articles.summary: Young actress Mamitha Baiju has received praise from Australian MP Brad Battin after attending an Onam celebration for the Malayali community in Australia.
articles.body: Young actress Mamitha Baiju has received praise from Australian MP Brad Battin after attending an Onam celebration for the Malayali community in Australia. The actress was the chief guest at the event, where she joined members of the Malayali diaspora to celebrate the festival.Brad Battin shared a selfie with Mamitha Baiju on his Instagram account and praised her humble nature. “What an honour to share the stage for Onam with @mamitha_baiju on her visit to Casey. A very down-to-earth, humble and beautiful superstar. Thank you Clyde Malayalee - Onashamsakal!” he wrote.Mamitha Baiju in AustraliaFor the unversed, the ‘BKU’ actress attended the Onam celebrations organised by the Clyde Malayali Association in Australia. The event was initially scheduled for September but had to be postponed after the actress was hospitalised with a high fever.Following her recovery, the celebrations were rescheduled for October. Mamitha had promised to visit Australia and participate in the event once she was feeling better. Keeping her word, the actress travelled to Australia after recovering.Mamitha Baiju’s recent and upcoming filmsThe actress has been enjoying a strong phase in her career, with several of her recent films performing well at the box office. Her recent projects include Tamil actor Vijay’s ‘Jana Nayagan’, Suriya-starrer ‘Vishwanath And Sons’ and the Malayalam film ‘Bethlehem Kudumba Unit’, which features Nivin Pauly and has been reported as a major box-office success.Her upcoming projects include ‘Irandu Vaanam’, the tentatively titled ‘PRS01’ and the Malayalam film ‘Hello Dear’.Mamitha Baiju’s reported Telugu debutMeanwhile, Mamitha has also been in the news following a report by 123Telugu suggesting that she is expected to make her Telugu debut with the mythological action drama ‘Jai Hanuman’. Directed by Prasanth Varma, the film stars Rishab Shetty in the lead role.However, neither the makers nor the actress has made an official announcement regarding her reported involvement in the project.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 2012, Taylor Swift donated $4 million to Nashville’s country music museum; 14 years later, its education centre gives local artists a platform
articles.summary: Discover how Taylor Swift's generous donation to the Country Music Hall of Fame has transformed an education center into a platform for local artists, including students and individuals with developmental disabilities, showcased in the 'Connection' exhibition.
articles.body: Taylor Swift’s $4 million contribution to Nashville’s Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum helped establish an education centre designed to make music history more interactive. Fourteen years later, the space is highlighting a different kind of talent, with a new exhibition featuring artwork by local school students and artists with developmental disabilities.Titled ‘Connection’, the exhibition opened in April 2026 at the Taylor Swift Education Centre. It features posters created by students from Metro Nashville Public Schools and artists associated with Friends Life Community, a nonprofit that supports adults with developmental disabilities. The project was developed in partnership with Hatch Show Print, the museum’s historic letterpress shop.In its official announcement on April 2, 2026, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum explained that participants explored the printing shop’s history and learned how to turn their ideas into posters. The finished pieces reflect themes including empathy, relationships and social causes, using words and images to communicate messages that matter to their creators.How did students and artists create their posters?Students from Cane Ridge High School, Hume-Fogg High School, Stratford High School and Nashville School of the Arts took part in a workshop at Hatch Show Print. They explored the shop’s collection, learned about poster design and experimented with printing shapes made from foam and sponges.The workshop gave them a chance to try a traditional printing technique rather than simply learn about it. Their experiments helped shape the posters displayed in the exhibition, with each participant bringing a personal idea to the project.Artists from Friends Life Community also contributed their work. Grant, Meghan and Sam collaborated with Jennifer Haston, the organisation’s visual arts programme coordinator, and Jim Sherraden, Hatch Show Print’s master printer emeritus.The resulting collection brings together different styles and perspectives. Some posters use lettering and colour to communicate a message, while others rely on imagery to express an idea. Displaying the works side by side gives visitors a glimpse of how differently people can interpret a shared theme.The centre behind the exhibitionSwift’s donation supported the museum’s capital campaign and helped make the education centre possible. The two-storey facility opened in 2013 and offers classrooms, a studio, an interactive gallery and spaces for educational activities.Its programmes introduce students and families to country music through hands-on experiences, including art-making and songwriting. The museum has also used the centre to showcase artwork by young people, giving students opportunities to respond to its collections and collaborate with local artists.‘Connection’ builds on that work by bringing school students and artists associated with Friends Life Community into the same exhibition. It also expands the centre’s focus beyond learning about music, showing how creative activities can help participants develop new skills and share their ideas with the public.A place for local voicesThe exhibition offers a look at what can happen when a cultural institution works with schools and community organisations. Participants were able to learn a traditional craft, make something of their own and see their work displayed in a public setting.For the museum, the project adds another chapter to the education centre’s ongoing programme of workshops and exhibitions. For visitors, it provides an opportunity to discover artwork shaped by the experiences and viewpoints of people from across Nashville.According to the museum’s official exhibition page, ‘Connection’ is scheduled to remain on display until spring 2027, with admission included in museum tickets.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: White House official defends Teresa Giudice’s visit as critics slam reality star’s ex-husband’s pardon push
articles.summary: Lynne Patton shared her cocaine addiction story and the intervention by Eric Trump and Lara Trump that shaped her belief in second chances for Joe Giudice.
articles.body: A senior White House official with longstanding ties to "The Real Housewives of New Jersey" star Teresa Giudice is addressing whether her ex-husband, Joe Giudice, deserves a second chance, while emphasizing that any presidential pardon decision rests solely with President Donald Trump. Lynne Patton, deputy assistant to the president for coalition policy and engagement, took to Instagram to explain why Teresa Giudice and her daughter, Gia Giudice, were invited to the White House for Columbus Day and Italian American heritage celebrations. Patton's comments about Joe, who was deported to Italy after serving time for fraud-related offenses, also addressed the family's efforts to secure a presidential pardon. ‘RHONJ’ ALUM JOE GIUDICE SAYS HE SHOULDN’T HAVE BEEN DEPORTED AFTER FRAUD CONVICTION Patton emphasized that she has no authority over presidential pardons but offered a personal message about redemption and second chances. "For those inquiring @teresagiudice and her daughter, @_giagiudice, were at the White House at the invitation of the President & First Lady in honor of Columbus Day & Italian-American heritage. I have known Teresa and her family, including @joe.giudice, for nearly two decades," Patton began her post. "I’ve attended family gatherings at their former New Jersey homes where Joe taught me how to roll meatballs & Teresa’s beloved father once showed me how to make his famous homemade wine. I am not in charge of pardons. Nor do I decide who receives them." She added, "That is the President’s sole decision based upon recommendations from the White House Pardon Czar, @alicemariefree, and White House Counsel." Patton then shared her own experience with addiction and the second chance she said the Trump family gave her. Patton said she relapsed into cocaine addiction while working at the Trump Organization in 2013, crediting Eric Trump and Lara Trump with staging an intervention that she said saved her life. Her experience, she said, shaped her belief in second chances. "To date, I have been drug-free for 13 years. They could have fired me. But instead, they told me that I was worth saving. Even when I didn’t believe that myself. Instead of sidelining me, they gave me more responsibility. I worked harder. Stayed in the office longer. Arrived earlier. More importantly, I earned back their trust & friendship. In turn, that translated into more self-confidence and earned promotions — including a personal request from their father to join him in D.C. It rebuilt my determination to succeed & help others do the same." Patton also cited her Christian faith and the importance of a father's presence in his children's lives. TODD AND JULIE CHRISLEY HOME FOR HOLIDAYS AFTER TRUMP PARDONS END PRISON TIME "With that said, my faith in God compels me to believe that a father’s place is in the home. Statistics confirm the same. More importantly, so does the Bible. Charlie Kirk often declared that the biblical role of the father to his child is to be their protector, both physically and spiritually. Quality time is everything. And no, it is never too late to be the provider who God intended every father to be," Patton added. "Do I believe that Joe deserves a second chance? Unfortunately, it is not my place to decide. But what I do know is that one of his beautiful daughters desperately needs him now more than ever. And even God supports that." Joe was deported to Italy in 2019 after serving 41 months in federal prison for financial crimes. He has been living in the Bahamas, while his four daughters remain in the United States. Gia has publicly advocated for her father's return to the United States. Joe sought a presidential pardon in June 2025, and Gia said in August 2026 that the family had filed a humanitarian packet as part of its efforts to bring him home. A presidential pardon would not automatically guarantee Joe's return to the United States. According to the Justice Department, a pardon can eliminate certain grounds for deportation, but its immigration consequences depend on the circumstances of the case. Gia wrote, "thank you Lynn♥️🙏🏼," while her sister Milania commented, "thank you so much ❤️." Teresa wrote, "We go way back ❤️," adding, "Love you ❤️." However, Patton's remarks drew mixed reactions from Instagram users. One Instagram user wrote, "What a beautiful post! That man did his time! Let him come home to his beautiful daughters!! Where he belongs!!!" "I hope Joe is able to come back! They allow all these illegals here with no consequences, and most of them are repeat offenders and dangerous. Bring @joe.giudice home to his family," wrote another. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? Sorry but this nepotism and bravolebrity entitlement does not put him above the law." "Explain how you pardon someone who isn’t a citizen. I care more about the affordability crisis than I do Bravo and Joe Guidice," another Instagram user said. Patton's Instagram post included photos documenting her ties to the Giudice family and the Trump administration. One image showed Patton posing for a mirror selfie at what appeared to be the White House. Another showed Teresa and Gia seated on an ornate blue-and-gold sofa inside a formal White House room. articles.title: ‘Breaking Bad’ star RJ Mitte’s cause of death revealed as co-stars Bryan Cranston, Aaron Paul mourn actor
articles.summary: RJ Mitte's representative confirmed the "Breaking Bad" actor and cerebral palsy advocate died by suicide at his Brownsville, Texas, home. He was 34.
articles.body: This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255). RJ Mitte, best known for playing Walter White Jr. on "Breaking Bad," died by suicide, his representative confirmed to Fox News Digital. He was 34. "Sadly, we can confirm that suicide was the cause of death," the representative said. The actor and disability rights advocate, who was diagnosed with cerebral palsy as a child, died Monday at his home in Brownsville, Texas, according to authorities. HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026: PHOTOS "It is with profound sadness we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte," Mitte's representative told Fox News Digital at the time. "Beyond entertaining friends and family around the world, he served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s." The statement noted that Mitte also served as president of The Mitte Foundation, which supports philanthropic efforts and community initiatives, while using his platform to challenge stereotypes and promote greater representation for people with disabilities. The Cameron County Justice of the Peace previously said an autopsy would be conducted. The actor’s death prompted an outpouring of grief from his former "Breaking Bad" co-stars, including Bryan Cranston, who played his on-screen father, Walter White. Cranston also praised Mitte’s work as a disability rights advocate and said they had remained close after the AMC series ended. The actor revealed that he and Mitte had recently discussed meeting for lunch, writing that he wondered whether such a meeting "would have changed his future." "But I do know that I loved him," Cranston wrote. "I’ll miss you, son." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? I have a very finite amount of time," Mitte said during the episode, which was released Oct. 5. Mitte also said the greatest gift of "Breaking Bad" was the platform it gave him to advocate for people with disabilities. "That’s really the greatest thing that ‘Breaking Bad’ has given me, is to be able to lend my voice to causes that make a meaningful impact that changes people’s lives," he said. articles.title: 'Jon & Kate' star Collin Gosselin claims mother zip-tied and locked him in basement room as a child
articles.summary: Collin Gosselin alleges mom Kate Gosselin zip-tied him, locked him in a basement room, and had him placed in an institution days before his 12th birthday.
articles.body: Collin Gosselin reflected on the alleged abuse he suffered at the hands of his mother, Kate Gosselin. Collin, 22, claimed in an interview with ABC that his mom allegedly made him sleep in a locked room in the basement as a way to isolate him from his father, Jon Gosselin. He claimed that one of his teachers noticed he had a swollen earlobe, which Collin said happened after Kate allegedly "dragged" him across the room by his ear during one abusive incident. 'JON & KATE PLUS 8' REALITY STAR'S TELL-ALL MEMOIR FOLLOWS YEARS OF ABUSE ALLEGATIONS "My teacher saw ... and then I talked to my guidance counselor, and I told them about it," Collin said. "And my mom was not very happy that I spoke about that." He was eventually pulled from school in the fourth grade, and recalled being "too afraid to say anything" when child protective services questioned abuse allegations. COLLIN GOSSELIN SENDS CRYPTIC SIGNAL TO MOM KATE AFTER CLAIMS SHE'S 'SPIRALING' OVER HIS UPCOMING MEMOIR Gosselin admitted he wasn't sure about life before the cameras arrived at his home to film his family, and told the outlet, "Simply put, my whole life that I lived was a lie." After one attempt to runaway, Collin claimed his mother allegedly zip-tied him and locked him in his basement room. KATE GOSSELIN CALLED A 'MONSTER' IN SOCIAL MEDIA COMMENTS AFTER SON COLLIN ANNOUNCES MEMOIR "She had put my wrists together ... and my ankles, and took black zip ties and zip-tied my hands and feet together," he alleged to the outlet. Days before his 12th birthday, Collin claimed Kate had him removed from their home and placed him in an institution. He alleged he was then "pumped with medication" and received little contact from his family. "I was told, 'This is for your own good,'" he recalled before admitting, "I threatened my mom's income, I threatened her image and people will do anything to protect their reputation, especially my mom." Kate claimed through the years that Collin suffered from a number of behavioral challenges. Collin wrote that she claimed he had autism, bipolar and obsessive compulsive disorder, but an independent psychological evaluation allegedly showed he didn't have any of those diagnoses. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "Everybody was like, 'Were you surprised when you got this?' I was like, 'No,'" he said. "Because I knew that, it's just that I needed it on paper." In a sit-down with Jay Shetty ahead of the release of his memoir, "In The Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood,' Collin claimed his earliest memories were when camera crews took over his house. "We were rolling every day, I mean at least a majority of the week, every week of the month of the year," he said. "And they were always there. There was always lights set up and cameras. And then once it got big enough and it was, it became, it went from ... you know, the big family in the small humble house to the big house." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Gosselin recalled the first indication that life "wasn't normal for a child" when his parents went through a divorce. "It was never normal," Gosselin noted. "That should never be a thing where you exploit children, where you film them potty training. But when I first had that recollection that ... realization, it was when my parents divorced and I kind of overheard some conversations where my father didn't want that for his children." Once they got all the pictures, we'd still want to play with the puppies ... and they'd take the puppies away." View this post on Instagram A post shared by Collin Gosselin (@collingosselin1) Fox News Digital has reached out to Kate's reps for comment. While Kate has remained quiet about the allegations, she defended herself over the summer on social media. The former reality TV star responded to comments on her TikTok posts referencing a few of Collin's claims where he alleged she "forced" him and his seven siblings apart and "pitted them against each other" as they were growing up. "If you are 100% certain that the accusations against you are lies, my suggestion would be to take him to court and sue him for defamation!" one fan asked. She responded, ""I can’t bc I’m a public figure. Rules are different unfortunately. Or I def would!" CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP She wrote on another post, "Malice is one of the hardest things to prove. I tried :(. The rules are different for ppl in the public eye." Gosselin also shared that she "consulted a high power LA attorney" in the past "when other ppl were putting crazy stuff out there," and that is what they told her. "The courts don’t honor it if you’re in the public eye :(" she added. She later responded to another comment, saying, "Sadly, Only parents who have a mentally ill child understand! It’s so tough and I’m learning that ppl have NO ability to understand unless they’ve been through it themselves."

articles.title: María del Monte, sobre su sexualidad: "Nunca he estado en un armario: primero porque no quepo y segundo porque no he tenido la necesidad"
articles.standfirst: La cantante ha sido la invitado de Pablo Motos este martes en 'El Hormiguero'
articles.summary: La cantante ha sido la invitado de Pablo Motos este martes en 'El Hormiguero'
articles.body: Pablo Motos ha recibido este martes en el plató de 'El Hormiguero' a la cantante María del Monte, quien ha presentado el libro 'Si el corazón se equivoca, se le perdona', sus memorias. En el mismo, la artista andaluza habla de sus aprendizajes, errores y aciertos que han formado parte de su intensa vida y larga trayectoria profesional. PABLO MOTOS. Vienes a presentarnos 'Si el corazón se equivoca, se le perdona', ¿por qué dices eso? MARÍA DEL MONTE. El corazón no suele equivocarse, pero si lo hace, se le perdona, porque siempre lo has hecho de corazón, aunque te equivoques. Yo soy de perdonar siempre, sobre todo porque me hace mal a mí misma guardar rencor, pero mi perdón tiene memoria. Las cosas que me dañan el alma son las que más cuesta perdonar. PABLO MOTOS. Dices que mirando a los ojos a la gente sabes cómo son, que los ojos son piscinas. MARÍA DEL MONTE. Hay piscinas que te pueden engañar, que parecen cristalinas, pero luego no lo son. Es verdad que, cuando miras a los ojos a las personas, sabes rápido si te dejan mirar dentro o si se echan para atrás. PABLO MOTOS. Dices en tu libro que tu padre no discutía nunca. MARÍA DEL MONTE. Sí, mi padre, que era un hombre muy sabio, decía que no había que discutir nunca en la vida, y que, las discusiones, se evitan con un puntito, con un puntito en la boca se refería. Qué suerte he tenido de tener los padres que me han tocado. PABLO MOTOS. Como a los 10 años tuviste una experiencia con la muerte. MARÍA DEL MONTE. Sí, con 10 años estaba medio dormida con mi madre, y ella estaba hablando con mi tía Aurora sobre alguien a quien habían enterrado, me desperté de un salto gritando que no me quería morir. Me tiré un año llorando porque no me quería morir, no comía ni nada. Me llevaron al médico porque estaban asustados. Se me fue pasando con el tiempo, pero me quedó un pequeño trauma, yo al cementerio no voy nunca, iré una sola vez, cuando me lleven para no volver. PABLO MOTOS. En el libro hablas sobre cuando falleció tu hermano y decidiste no contárselo a tu madre. MARÍA DEL MONTE. Sí, me llamó mi hermano mayor por teléfono, para darme la noticia, y tenía sentada al lado a mi madre, que tenía noventa años. Tuve que disimular para no contárselo y me pasé año y medio engañándola, diciéndole que mi hermano estaba bien cada vez que me preguntaba. Dudaba si estaba haciendo bien o no, en no contárselo. Ese estado de ansiedad prolongada durante tanto tiempo, para mí fue terrorífico. PABLO MOTOS. Tú dices que has visto y sentido a personas fallecidas. MARÍA DEL MONTE. He sentido perfectamente a mi hermano en mi casa, le he olido. Pero no solo yo, mi madre, antes de morir, decía que veía a mi padre y a mi hermano ya fallecidos por casa, ella me decía: "Les veo, pero no como a ti, les veo diferente". PABLO MOTOS. Cuando estuviste la vez anterior, dijiste que España iba a ganar el Mundial y ganó. Ahora te pregunto, ¿quién va a ganar las elecciones? MARÍA DEL MONTE. Las elecciones creo que no las va a ganar ningún partido político, solo le pido a Dios que no perdamos nosotros. Yo no sé de política, pero creo que la primera misión de los políticos es velar por los intereses del país, mirando por los ciudadanos, no por ellos. PABLO MOTOS. Hay quien dice que dijiste públicamente que eras lesbiana una vez que murió tu madre. ¿Te has sentido alguna vez dentro de un armario? MARÍA DEL MONTE. Nunca, y tengo dos argumentos maravillosos: uno, que no quepo, y otro, que no he tenido la necesidad. Yo no he vivido una infancia ni una juventud reprimida, siempre he tenido mucha libertad en mi entorno. Mi madre ha sabido siempre cómo era su hija; ¿cómo no va a conocer una madre a sus hijos?

articles.title: Tupac Shakur murder case: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis gets 40 years to life in prison for orchestrating rapper's death
articles.summary: Duane \"Keffe D\" Davis was sentenced Tuesday to 40 years to life in prison for orchestrating the murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur who was gunned down off
articles.body: Duane "Keffe D" Davis was sentenced Tuesday to 40 years to life in prison for orchestrating the murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur who was gunned down off the Las Vegas Strip over 30 years ago.Davis, 63, was convicted in August of first-degree murder with the use of a deadly weapon. He is the only person ever charged in the death of Shakur, whose popularity was peaking at age 25.Prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo said Tuesday that whatever sentence the court imposes, Davis is "guaranteed to die" behind bars."It's not just about losing a family member," DiGiacomo said as Shakur's sister Sekyiwa "Set" Shakur nods her head in the audience.The killing went unsolved for years until Davis, a former leader of the South Side Compton Crips, gave interviews and published his role in the shooting in his 2019 tell-all memoir.DiGiacomo said Davis was trying to profit off a killing that he committed, and for that he does not deserve the minimum sentence."In my mind he deserves the maximum possible sentence," DiGiacomo said.Davis spoke briefly in court, telling Judge Carli Kierny he wants items back that police took from his house, including his pictures. Asked if there was anything else he wanted to say, Davis said: "No I'm good."Davis' lawyer, Michael Sanft said he plans to appeal the verdict. Sanft said prosecutors waited too long to bring the case.On the night of Sept. 7, 1996, Shakur was in the passenger seat of a black BMW with music mogul Marion "Suge" Knight when a white Cadillac pulled up at a red light, and shots erupted. Shakur was shot multiple times and died six days later, while Knight survived.Shakur is considered one of the most influential and versatile rappers of all time and had a burgeoning film career as an actor at the time of his death. His legend has only grown since. His songs still resonate among fans with themes of hardship, love and Black struggles.In his memoir, Davis explained how Shakur and his entourage beat up Davis' nephew hours before the shooting in Las Vegas. He said he sought retaliation, and that he was in the passenger seat of the Cadillac and passed the gun to the backseat, where shots were fired. Davis had spoken to detectives years before but avoided prosecution because of an agreement he made with law enforcement.During the weekslong trial, prosecutors relied on Davis' own statements he made to law enforcement and documentarians. They argued Davis orchestrated the shooting and provided the gun used in Shakur's death, which was the result of a rivalry between the South Side Compton Crips and Mob Piru. Davis' defense attorney pointed to a lack of physical evidence that connected his client to the 30-year-old crime, and he portrayed Davis as a liar who was trying to make money.After nine days of hearing testimony in August, the jury deliberated for three hours before turning over the guilty verdict.Shakur was an icon, a brotherShakur's family spoke at the sentencing, including his siblings Maurice "Mopreme" Shakur and Sekyiwa "Set" Shakur.Following the verdict, prosecutor Binu Palal said that to many people, Shakur was an icon or an idea, "but to the family, Tupac Shakur was a brother, a son, a cousin, a loved person ripped from them 30 years ago."Palal said the family had to sit through years of Davis "bragging about killing someone they loved.""They loved that man. And the arrogance that Mr. Davis had in expressing his joy in killing that man ultimately was his undoing," Palal said.Prosecutors say they have insufficient evidence to charge anyone elseDavis is the only person to be charged and convicted in the killing of Shakur. The three other people who allegedly were in the Cadillac - including Davis' nephew Orlando "Baby Lane" Anderson who Davis said was the one who pulled the trigger - have died.Sean "Diddy" Combs and his alleged role were brought up often throughout the trial. Witnesses testified Combs used members of the South Side Compton Crips for security for Bad Boy Records. In his book and public statements, Davis alleged Combs offered him money to kill Shakur and Knight. Combs, who is serving a four-year prison sentence after being convicted of prostitution-related offenses, has repeatedly denied any involvement in the death of Shakur.Clark County District Attorney Steve Wolfson has said his office doesn't believe it has sufficient evidence to charge anyone else."But like any other case, if we come into more information, more evidence, we can always consider filing additional charges," he said following the guilty verdict. "But today, we don't believe that's the appropriate move to make."Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Actress Amanda Seyfried rejected TV role over nonstop sex scenes, refused to get 'naked with a stranger'
articles.summary: Amanda Seyfried says she's no longer willing to be naked with strangers on set, joining Hollywood actresses pushing back against intimate scene demands.
articles.body: Actress Amanda Seyfried revealed during a Sunday conversation with Alec Baldwin at the Hamptons International Film Festival in East Hampton, New York, that she rejected a television series because of its frequent sex scenes, explaining that she has become increasingly uncomfortable performing intimate scenes as she gets older. "I passed on a show where I would have to have sex all the time because of the sex. Doesn't matter [who it's with]… I don't want to do it. I'm uncomfortable with it. I'm not into it right now," Seyfried said, according to People Magazine. Seyfried's decision echoes concerns raised by other Hollywood actresses, including Gina Gershon, who told Fox News Digital in March that she rejected a starring role in the 1981 horror film "Friday the 13th Part 2" after learning her character would appear topless. "I was offered a lead in that movie," Gershon said, adding that the nudity "definitely felt kind of exploitative to me." 'GAME OF THRONES' STAR LENA HEADEY SAYS OUTRAGE OVER INFAMOUS NUDE SCENE LEFT HER STUNNED Seyfried, 40, said her feelings about portraying romantic relationships on screen have changed significantly since the beginning of her career, when she was more enthusiastic about filming intimate scenes. "Maybe if [the project] came along again [at a later point], maybe I'd be in a different space. But I don't want to deal with being naked with a stranger," Seyfried said. The Oscar-nominated actress previously acknowledged feeling pressured to participate in uncomfortable scenes when she was younger. In a 2022 interview with Porter magazine, Seyfried described participating in scenes without underwear at 19 because she feared upsetting people and jeopardizing her career. "Oh, I know why: I was 19, and I didn't want to upset anybody and I wanted to keep my job. That's why," Seyfried said. SYDNEY SWEENEY DEFENDS 'EUPHORIA' NUDITY AND REVEALS A POLE DANCING SCENE WAS CUT FROM SEASON THREE Other actresses have described similar experiences. In 2023, Christina Ricci revealed on "The View" that she was once threatened with legal action after refusing to perform an intimate scene in a particular way. "Someone threatened to sue me once because I didn't want to do this sex scene in a certain way," Ricci said. Keira Knightley previously revealed that becoming a mother changed her willingness to appear nude on camera. The actress incorporated a no-nudity clause into her contracts, allowing her greater control over intimate scenes. CATE BLANCHETT MOURNS HOW #METOO GOT 'KILLED VERY QUICKLY,' STILL 'SYSTEMIC LAYER OF ABUSE' Not every actress has taken the same approach. In June, Fox News Digital reported that "Euphoria" star Sydney Sweeney rejected creator Sam Levinson's suggestion to reduce nudity in the show's third season, believing the scenes were relevant to her character's storyline. Hollywood has introduced additional protections for actors filming intimate scenes. Jessica Steinrock, an intimacy coordinator, told Fox News Digital that coordinators help establish expectations and consent during production. "[Intimacy Coordinator] is a relatively new role. It really hit its stride kind of in 2018 when HBO made their commitment to having an intimacy coordinator on all their film sets," she said. "An intimacy coordinator is there to provide safety and framework for scenes of intimacy. Those are scenes of simulated sex, simulated genital contact, or scenes of nudity." CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Under SAG-AFTRA's guidelines, performers must receive advance notice of expected nudity or simulated sex acts, and producers generally must provide written nudity riders at least 48 hours before filming. The union also established a collective bargaining agreement covering intimacy coordinators in 2025. Seyfried, who shares two children with actor Thomas Sadoski, said motherhood has further influenced her willingness to establish boundaries, both professionally and personally.
